questions.q: What is the elevator governor for?
o: Detecting overspeed and tripping the safety gear
Controlling how fast the doors open
Levelling the car with each floor
Balancing the car against the counterweight
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The governor turns with the car on its own rope. At overspeed it cuts power, then grips its rope, which pulls the safety gear onto the rails.

questions.q: What does the door operator do?
o: Drives the traction sheave
Opens and closes the car door, which drives the hoistway door with it
Locks the hoistway door when the car is away
Reopens the door when a passenger is in the way
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The door operator is a motor on top of the car. The interlock locks the doors, and the safety edge or light curtain reopens them.

questions.q: What is the vertical enclosure in which an elevator car travels called?
o: Machine room
Elevator lobby
Hoistway
Plenum
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The hoistway (shaft) holds the car, counterweight, rails and ropes, from the pit to the overhead.

questions.q: What does the traveling cable do?
o: Carries the weight of the car
Trips the safety gear at overspeed
Balances the weight of the hoist ropes
Carries power and signals between the moving car and the building
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The traveling cable hangs in a loop from mid-hoistway to the car. The hoist ropes carry the car, the governor rope trips the safety, and compensating chains balance rope weight.

o: Guide the car and counterweight and give the safety gear something to grip
Carry the weight of the car down to the pit
Hold the hoistway doors in line
Carry electric power to the car
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Steel T-rails run the full height of the shaft. Guide shoes or rollers on the car run along them.

questions.q: Which two doors does an elevator entrance have?
o: A car door and a fire door
A car door and a hoistway (landing) door
A landing door and a machine-room door
A hoistway door and a pit door
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The car door travels with the car. Each floor has its own hoistway door, which the car door opens when the car arrives.

questions.q: What does the brake on a traction machine do?
o: Levels the car with the floor before the doors open
Grips the guide rails when the car overspeeds
Stops the drive and holds the car still at a floor
Absorbs the impact at the bottom of the pit
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The brake is spring-applied and held off electrically, so it sets whenever power is lost.

o: In the machine room, beside the brake
On top of the car, above the crosshead
In the lobby, behind the hall call buttons
In the pit, below the car and the counterweight
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Spring or oil buffers stop a car or counterweight that runs past the bottom landing.

o: The grooved drive wheel that moves the ropes by friction
An idler pulley that only redirects the ropes
A wheel on the car that runs along the rail
A drum that winds up the rope
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The ropes run over the sheave to the car on one side and the counterweight on the other. Friction in the grooves moves them.

questions.q: What is the space in the hoistway above the top landing called?
o: Pit
Overhead
Travel
Sill
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The overhead gives clearance for the car and its equipment if it runs past the top landing.

questions.q: What does the elevator controller do?
o: Drives the ropes directly
Absorbs the impact in the pit
Answers calls and controls the drive, doors and safety circuits
Grips the rails at overspeed
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The controller is the brain: it registers calls, dispatches cars, starts and stops the motor, and runs the doors.

questions.q: What does the safety gear of an elevator do?
o: Absorbs the energy of the car in the pit
Detects overspeed and signals the controller
Holds the drive sheave when the car is parked
Grips the guide rails to stop the car when it overspeeds
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The safety gear is under the car. When the governor trips it, wedges clamp the rails and stop the car.

questions.q: What is the counterweight in a traction elevator for?
o: Balancing the car plus about 40–50% of rated load, so the motor does less work
Holding the car if all the ropes break
Keeping the ropes taut in the pit
Stopping the car at the top landing
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: With the car half loaded, the two sides nearly balance and the motor only has to overcome friction.

questions.q: The space below the lowest landing level in the hoistway is called the:
o: Overhead
Machine deck
Sill pocket
Pit
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The pit is the part of the hoistway below the lowest landing. It holds the buffers.

questions.q: What does a door interlock do?
o: Reopens the door when a passenger is in the way
Holds the doors open during fire-service operation
Keeps the car from moving unless the hoistway door is closed and locked
Levels the car before the doors open
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Each hoistway door has an interlock that locks it unless the car is there and breaks the safety circuit if it is open.
